note: Calque: »et sødt stykke arbejde« is an anglicism for »a sweet piece of work«.
Non-standard spelling »forderve«; correct form is »fordærve«.
Garbled comparative »som nogen nogensinde har vendt om og stukket af«.
Missing comma before subordinate clause (»Især ikke, da ...«); reads ambiguously.
Address inconsistent: the King uses »du« to his lords in this scene (Worcester, Westmoreland), not »De«.
"kæmpet med" ambiguous (= alongside); calque "tage ... op som fjende"; mixed De/I address to Northumberland in one breath
"pressede ham om at" unidiomatic
"lever ... i dårligt omdømme" unidiomatic
"vær så venlig" stiff calque of "please"; title form per guide
missing preposition: "plet at have" -> "plet ved at have"
ungrammatical "hvis du ikke er" (needs "det")
Worcester addresses his brother with De; brothers use du in this scene (Bror/gode bror)
"ligeværdigt" (as equals) is wrong sense of "evenly"
"Han" ambiguous, reads as the farmer; English "That one" = the companion
pun on "man" breaks: previous line says "ærlig mand", here "menneske"
mistranslation: "ikke snydt for en hest" (not cheated of a horse) contradicts the joke; the colted/uncolted explanation is dropped
"opsporet" (tracked down) ≠ "set up"
Wrong gender: sukker(et) is neuter, so 'for den' must be 'for det'.
Inconsistent running gag: »Coming« is rendered »Straks« elsewhere (incl. the Prince's setup); use Straks.
Echo of Francis's word must match »Straks« used for »Coming« throughout the scene.
Number wrong: 'half a dozen' is et halvt dusin, not en halv snes (ten).
Poins mimics Francis's »Coming«, rendered »Straks« elsewhere; keep consistent.
Referent: crickets are fårekyllinger, not græshopper.
»Coming« rendered »Straks« elsewhere in the scene; keep consistent.
Follows older wording: the parenthetical '(soft-hearted sun god!)' qualifies the sun god, not the butter.
'udgydt' means poured out/shed, not spawned; a spawned-out herring is a sild, der har gydt.
Follows older English: omits 'their other points, the laces holding up their pants, broke too'.
Non-word »hesteryggerbrækker«; compound is »hesterygbrækker«.
»få vejret igen et stykke tid« mixes a one-off result with a duration; stiff.
Calque »som noget« (as anything).
Loses »I knew it was you ... as God did«; Danish reads as knowing them as well as he knows God.
Prince addressing the Hostess (an inferior) should use »du«, not »De«.
Peto uses »dig« to the Prince while Bardolph uses »De« in the same scene; inconsistent address.
»sværge sig troskab« makes the devil swear loyalty to himself (wrong referent); »pike« reads as »girl« in Danish, not the weapon.
Calque »en kraftig en« (a stout one).
»den bøllernes fader« is ungrammatical (demonstrative plus s-genitive).
Calque »som den næste mand« (as the next man).
English says the King speaks of Hotspur by that name; Danish says he hears the name (older/different detail).
Calque »uden noget at vise for det«.
Follows older English (»giver mig samme fordel«); English says it curves just as far up into my land on the other side.
»Tja« softens Glendower's firm reply.
»viseagenter« is not idiomatic for ballad-peddlers; »skære i tænderne« not a Danish idiom.
»holdt han mig hen« means stalled me, not kept me; »nagende kone« is a calque.
V2 word order: »Ærligt talt, min herre, du er«.
Mortimer addresses Glendower as »du« elsewhere in the scene; »Deres« is inconsistent.
»jeg slækker aldrig« is ungrammatical (slække needs an object/på).
»i seng med« changes the line; English: help me to the Welsh lady's bed.
»solklar« means obvious, not sun-like; »omgås bærme« lacks the definite form.
Gender: »trods« is common gender (åben trods).
Garbled sentence split leaves a fragment (»Ja, selv den mindste ære ...«).
non-word »munt«; »bandede lidt« (swore a little) does not render »hardly ever swore«
garbled »det bælgmørke mørkes søn«; calque »hældning mod dyd«
calque »jeg trodser Dem« (I defy you)
broken word order »Nu, så sandt …, det var«
anglicism »en otte penny eller så«
stiff/garbled »modtagelig for enhver ærlig fornuft«
garbled »af denne årgangs prægning«
invented stage direction [Til Douglas.] not in the English
»mælkebøtter« means dandelions, not milksops; missing comma in »sige det, som det er«
'modtaget' means received, not accepted; an offer that is not accepted is 'ikke taget imod'.
Follows older English: 'Jo, af de døde' (yes, to the dead) reverses the current 'Not by the dead, no.'
"bruge den korte tid på skam" is unidiomatic for "spend that short time shamefully"
"vinde dagen" is an anglicism (win the day)
"så er den ikke længere" is garbled for "that’s the end of it"
"endnu en falsk" lacks a noun; "bære sig ad" means behave/manage, not "carry yourself"; V2 after "Og dog"
stiff relative construction "den uforskammede hånd, Douglas har"
"denne krudthoved" is a non-word with wrong gender; Danish "brushoved"
"give blod på tanden" means whet the appetite, not blood the sword
ungrammatical resumptive pronoun "Den, der belønner mig, må Gud belønne ham"
